name: Tsang Chih
bio: Tsang Chih lived in the sixth century. Waley prints a single four-line song of his, in the voice of a girl growing up under the walls of a castle.
The poems here are Arthur Waley’s version in A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918), given with the poet’s name as spelled in those books.

poems.title: Song
poems.author: Tsang Chih
poems.collection: A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918)
poems.text:
I was brought up under the Stone Castle:
My window opened on to the castle tower.
In the castle were beautiful young men
Who waved to me as they went in and out.
